limited_overlap.description: 0.7% of training applicants have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds; no single covariate region holds most of them.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (223 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 18,906 against 37,112; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: smsa p=0.232 (-9012, -21636, -2442, -9601 dollars per SD); prior_earnings p=0.281 (+40667, +91496, +7834, +45593 dollars per SD); age p=0.3 (-3754, -8451, -1080, -3847 dollars per SD); education p=0.337 (-2602, -4381, +186, -1731 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect 14,219 dollars with 90% interval [-13,358, 41,796], against the ATE 7,911. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,334.5 (train) against 25,350.1 (test); months_unemployed 2.6 (train) against 3.2 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 1.0%. 40 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 8,417 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 4.8%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['smsa', 'prior_earnings', 'age'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
